title: Windowed reassembly + hybrid-poll fallback for SSE streaming with deterministic structured-output reconstitution
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Clients occasionally observe corrupted or partial JSONL/structured outputs after reconnects when network interruptions interleave with server-side function/tool-calls. Current resume tokens and byte-offset heuristics are brittle across proxies and in the presence of intermediate transformers (e.g., edge rate limiters). This ticket designs and implements a graceful fallback path that: 1) reassembles SSE chunks deterministically using per-chunk integrity anchors, 2) negotiates a hybrid long-poll fallback when streaming cannot be resumed within a bounded window, and 3) preserves function-call/structured output atomicity during reconnect and replay so downstream consumers do not see half-invoked tool calls or truncated JSON objects.
proposal: Add a windowed reassembly protocol on top of SSE where each chunk is annotated with: a sequence window id, a content-hash anchor (SHA256 prefix), and an optional semantic-boundary hint header (e.g., JSONL-boundary, functioncall-start, functioncall-end). Clients and servers will negotiate a small feature set at handshake time (Accept-Streaming-Mode: full-resume | windowed | fallback-only). On reconnect, the client presents the last-seen window id and last anchor; the server attempts windowed fast-reconciliation up to N windows back. If reconciliation fails (mismatch or gaps beyond policy), the server offers a hybrid-poll fallback URL that returns a single consolidated payload for final reassembly. All tool/function calls are treated as atomic units: the server will never surface a tool-call result without the matching functioncall-end anchor. This ensures deterministic reconstitution of structured outputs across resume/fallback transitions.
design_notes: - Chunk metadata fields: window_id (int), seq_in_window (int), anchor_sha256_8 (8 hex chars), semantic_hint (enum: NONE|JSONL|FUNC_START|FUNC_END|TOOL_OUTPUT). These are transported as SSE event-level fields (prefixed headers) to remain compatible with existing SSE clients.
acceptance_criteria: - Server emits new per-chunk metadata for all streamed responses behind a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria_2: - Client library can resume using windowed reconciliation for up to 5 windows and successfully rehydrate structured JSONL outputs in automated tests.
acceptance_criteria_3: - If reconciliation fails, server returns a hybrid-poll fallback URL (https) and client fetches consolidated payload; tests validate identical final structured object compared to a uninterrupted stream.
acceptance_criteria_4: - Function/toolcall atomicity: no partial functioncall bodies are delivered; unit tests simulate mid-call disconnects and assert either full invocation or no invocation delivered.
implementation_plan: 1) Server: add chunk annotation generator and feature-flag gate. 2) Server: implement reconciliation endpoint that accepts last-window/anchor and attempts delta replay. 3) Server: implement hybrid-poll aggregator which can synthesize a consolidated final payload for clients that cannot resume. 4) Client SDK: add handshake header support, windowed-reassembly logic, and fallback fetcher. 5) Add E2E tests including flaky-network harness that simulates packet loss and delayed fragments. 6) Roll out behind feature flag, enable for internal customers, run canary traffic, then enable broadly.
implementation_notes: - Use incremental SHA256 (first 8 hex chars) for anchors to keep metadata small. - Keep anchors advisory; servers may use full hash for validation but only advertise prefix to avoid payload bloat. - Hybrid-poll fallback must be short-lived and rate-limited to avoid abuse; tie to request id and TTL.
qa_plan: - Unit tests for chunk encoding/decoding and anchor validation. - E2E: deterministic reassembly test matrix (single-chunk, chunk-split, out-of-order within window, multi-window gap, functioncall interrupted). - Load test: measure latency/regression for streaming with anchors enabled vs disabled. - Compatibility test: ensure legacy SSE clients ignore unknown event fields and still process text events (graceful degradation).
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Feature-flagged internal rollout (2 days) with telemetry for resume success rate and hybrid-poll invocations. Stage 2: Canary with 5% of external requests for 1 week, monitor error spikes and cost due to hybrid-poll. Stage 3: Gradual ramp to 100% and deprecate old resume heuristics after 30 days if stable.
risks_mitigation: - Risk: increased bandwidth from metadata; mitigate by keeping anchor short and optional semantic hints. - Risk: clients that strip SSE fields (proxies) break reconciliation; mitigation: hybrid-poll as deterministic fallback. - Risk: state explosion on server for delta windows; mitigation: bounded window retention policy and GC.
comments: 2025-02-14 Ava Chen: Initial ticket — outlined problem, proposal, and rough acceptance criteria. Assigned to Diego.

2025-02-15 Diego Morales: Spike completed — validated that adding small event-level headers doesn't break Node/browser EventSource. PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-replay-poc (PR #12).

2025-02-16 Diego Morales: Discovered one proxy (internal edge) strips event-level headers when 'text/event-stream' passes through our rate limiter. Added hybrid-poll fallback to proposal to cover this.

2025-02-17 Priya Nair (Security): Reviewed threat model — concern about anchors leaking content hash semantics across tenants. Recommendation: use per-request salt and truncate anchor to 8 chars. Marked security_review_required.

2025-02-18 Diego Morales: Implemented server-side chunk annotations behind ff: streaming.windowed_reassembly. Added reconcile endpoint at /v1/stream/reconcile and hybrid fallback at /v1/stream/fallback. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/3214 — in review.

2025-02-19 QA: Added flaky-network E2E harness tests. Found race where functioncall-end hint was emitted after last text chunk during abrupt cancel. Fix planned to ensure functioncall-end is always last event for atomicity.

2025-02-20 Diego Morales: Updated implementation to emit functioncall-end anchor deterministically before connection close; updated tests. Preparing canary rollout plan and telemetry dashboards (runtime/streaming/resume_success_rate).
2025-02-20 Product (Lina Ortega): Noted customer ask from FinServ pilot for strict audit logs on fallback usage. Added label and dependency PM-902 to coordinate audit requirement.
2025-02-20 Diego Morales: Requesting design review and sign-off from infra and SDK owners before canary. Linking RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Windowed+Stream+Reassembly+RFC
